'''Maurice René Michel Jacob''' ({{birth date |1933|03|28|df=yes}} – {{date of death|2007|05|02|df=yes}}) was a French [[Theoretical physics|theoretical particle physicist]].

== Biography ==
Maurice Jacob studied physics at [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] from 1953 to 1957. During a visit to the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in 1959, he developed with [[Gian-Carlo Wick]] the helicity formalism for relativistic  description  of  scattering  of  particles  with  spin  and  the  decay  of particles  and  resonant  states.<ref name="JacobWick1959">{{cite journal|last1=Jacob|first1=M.|last2=Wick|first2=G.C.|title=On the general theory of collisions for particles with spin|journal=Annals of Physics|volume=7|issue=4|year=1959|pages=404–428|issn=0003-4916|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(59)90051-X|bibcode=1959AnPhy...7..404J}}</ref> In 1961, he obtained a doctorate on this subject at the [[University of Paris]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Jacob |first=Maurice |year=1961 |title=Théorie formelle des collisions et états propres d'hélicité |type=PhD |url=https://inspirehep.net/record/896440/files/CM-P00070301.pdf}}</ref> His thesis advisors were professors [[Francis Perrin (physicist)|Francis Perrin]] and [[Gian-Carlo Wick]]. Jacob then moved, as a post-doctoral fellow, to [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]]. He worked in [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre|Saclay]] from 1961 to 1967. From 1967 he worked at [[CERN]] until his retirement in 1998. From 1982 to 1988, he headed the theoretical physics division of CERN and in the 1990s, he was responsible for CERN's relations with its Member States.<ref name=":0">
{{cite magazine |date=July–August 2007 |title=Maurice Jacob 1933–2007 |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734100  |magazine= CERN Courier |volume=47 |number=6|page=39 |location=Bristol |publisher=Institute of Physics}}</ref>

Maurice Jacob's research focuses on the phenomenology of strong interactions, including diffraction, scaling, high-transverse-momentum processes and the formation of [[quark–gluon plasma]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jacob|first1=M.|last2=Rafelski|first2=J.|author-link2=Johann Rafelski|year=1987|title=Longitudinal polarization, abundance and quark-gluon plasma formation|journal=Physics Letters B|language=en|volume=190|issue=1–2|pages=173–176|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(87)90862-8|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/175429}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Heinz|first1=Ulrich|last2=Jacob|first2=Maurice|date=2000-02-16|title=Evidence for a New State of Matter: An Assessment of the Results from the CERN Lead Beam Programme|eprint=nucl-th/0002042 }}</ref> In particular, he pioneered the studies of inclusive hadron-production processes, including scaling and its violations. He contributed also to the field of accelerator physics together with [[Tai Tsun Wu]].<ref name="JacobWu1993">{{cite journal|last1=Jacob|first1=M.|last2=Wu|first2=Tai Tsun|title=Transverse distribution effects in beamstrahlung|journal=Zeitschrift für Physik C|volume=58|issue=2|year=1993|pages=279–284|issn=0170-9739|doi=10.1007/BF01560346|bibcode=1993ZPhyC..58..279J|s2cid=121467413|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/241373}}</ref>

He supported [[Carlo Rubbia]] during the construction of the [[Super Proton Synchrotron]] (SPS) in the 1980s.<ref name="bulletin" /><ref name="Van HoveJacob1980">{{cite journal|last1=Van Hove|first1=L.|author-link=Léon Van Hove|last2=Jacob|first2=M.|year=1980|title=Highlights of 25 years of physics at CERN|journal=Physics Reports|volume=62|issue=1|pages=1–86|doi=10.1016/0370-1573(80)90103-9|bibcode=1980PhR....62....1V|issn=0370-1573}}</ref>

{{blockquote|Maurice Jacob played a key role in bringing together different groups from the experimental and theoretical nuclear and particle physics communities to initiate an ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collision program at the CERN SPS, in order to search for the quark-gluon plasma.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/78/02/028005| title=From SPS to RHIC: Maurice and the CERN heavy-ion programme| year=2008| last1=Heinz| first1=Ulrich W.| journal=Physica Scripta| volume=78| issue=2| article-number=028005| arxiv=0805.4572| bibcode=2008PhyS...78b8005H| s2cid=13833990}}</ref>}}

Jacob chaired the [[French Physical Society]] from 1985 to 2002 and from 1991 to 1993 he was president of the [[European Physical Society]]. In 1993, he became a member of the [[American Physical Society]]. He was co-editor of [[Physics Letters B]] and [[Physics Reports]].<ref name="Jacob1995">{{cite book|author=Maurice Jacob|title=In the Wings of Physics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WG8-z6arzyAC|year=1995|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-02-2178-2}}</ref>

He was appointed member of the [[CNRS]] scientific council in 1988.<ref>{{cite book | title = Portant nomination au conseil scientifique du centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS) | 
url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/affichTexte.do?cidTexte=JORFTEXT000000296546&categorieLien=id|date=10 March 1988}}</ref>

He was a corresponding member of the [[Academy of Sciences (France)|Academy of Sciences]] from 1977, member of the [[Swedish Royal Academies]] and also scientific advisor to the [[European Space Agency]].<ref>
{{cite web |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/academie/membre/Jacob_Maurice.htm |title=In memoriam: Maurice Jacob |author=Guy Laval|date=November 2007 |publisher=L'Académie des sciences |access-date=21 February 2020}}</ref>

== Marriage and children ==
Maurice Jacob was married to Lise Jacob. Together they have 4 children  Jimmy, Thierry, Francis, and [[Irène Jacob|Irène]].<ref name="bulletin">{{Cite news|last=Ellis|first=John|author-link=John Ellis (physicist, born 1946)|date=14 May 2007|title=CERN Bulletin|issue=20/2007 & 21/2007|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1033955|access-date=22 February 2020}}</ref>
